newsitem.title: USA: TWA revs, cash balance shrinks.
newsitem.headline: TWA revs, cash balance shrinks.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc posted a larger-than-expected second quarter loss, while revenues and cash balances declined.

TWA's second quarter loss of $0.31 excluding extraordinary items was greater than the $0.23 per share loss analysts had expected, according to First Call. During the year ago second quarter, TWA earned a profit of $0.46 a share.

The St. Louis-based airline's second quarter operating revenues dropped to $844 million from $965 million last year. The airline said the decline in revenue was due to a planned reduction in capacity from the ongoing replacement of 747 and L1011 aircraft with smaller 767 and 757 planes. During the quarter, scheduled system capacity dropped 9.1 percent.
TWA's cash balance at the end of the second quarter dropped to $102.6 million, down from $181.6 million as the end of 1996.

During the quarter, overall operating expenses declined to $838.5 million from $903.8 million due to a decline in fuel prices and fuel consumption. Operating expenses per available seat mile was 8.92 cents for the quarter, up from 8.71 cents a year ago.
Aircraft maintenance materials and repair expenses decreased as the airline operated newer planes which require less routine maintenance.
Payroll expenses fell about $5.2 million from a year ago. TWA employed about 23,490 workers at the end of the second quarter, down 1,605 from the end of last year.
Separately, TWA said Tuesday it would cut an additional 1,000 workers by December.
TWA also said it will improve services for its business travelers by expandinng first class cabins and improving the frequent flier program.
Shares of TWA lost 1/16 to 6-9/16 on the American Stock Exchange.
